App.Name: MonitorControl
Alert.IncompatibleVersion.Title: Incompatible previous version
Alert.IncompatibleVersion.Message: Settings for an incompatible previous app version detected. Default settings are reloaded.
Alert.SafeMode.Title: Safe Mode Activated
Alert.SafeMode.Message: Shift was pressed during launch. MonitorControl started in safe mode. Default settings are reloaded, DDC read is blocked.
Alert.GammaInterference.Title: Is f.lux or similar running?
Alert.GammaInterference.Message:
An other app seems to change the brightness or colors which causes issues.

To solve this, you need to quit the other app or disable gamma control for your displays in MonitorControl!
Alert.GammaInterference.DisableGamma: Disable gamma control for my displays
Alert.ResetSettings.Title: Reset Settings?
Alert.ResetSettings.Message: Are you sure you want to reset all settings?
Alert.LongerDelay.Title: Enable Longer Delay?
Alert.LongerDelay.Message: Are you sure you want to enable a longer delay? Doing so may freeze your system and require a restart. Start at login will be disabled as a safety measure.
Alert.ShortcutTaken.Title: This keyboard shortcut is already used by Windows or another app.
Notification.ShortcutConflicts: These MonitorControl shortcuts are also registered by another app: {0}
Update.Available.Title: A new version is available
Update.Available.Message: MonitorControl {0} is available (you have {1}). Install it now? The app will restart.
Update.UpToDate.Title: You're up to date!
Update.NotInstalled: Updates are only available when MonitorControl is installed with its installer.
Update.Failed: Unable to check for updates. Please try again later.
General.StartupAction.DoNothing: Assume last saved settings are valid (recommended)
General.StartupAction.Write: Apply last saved values to the display
General.StartupAction.DoNothingText: Use brightness, volume and other settings from last time or use defaults. Values will be applied to the display upon first change by the user.
General.StartupAction.WriteText: Useful when a display tends to reset its settings during sleep.
General.StartupAction.ReadText: Update settings from the display. May not work with some hardware.
General.CombinedText: Use software dimming after the display reached zero hardware brightness for extended range. Works for DDC controlled displays only.
General.AllowZero: Allow zero brightness via software or combined dimming
General.AllowZeroText: Warning! With this option enabled, you might find yourself in a position when you end up with a blank display. This, combined with disabled keyboard controls can be frustrating.
General.SmoothText: You can disable smooth transitions for a more direct, immediate control.
General.Sync: Sync brightness changes from built-in displays
General.SyncText: Changes caused by adaptive brightness or made with the laptop brightness keys, Quick Settings or Windows Settings will be replicated to all displays.
General.SafeModeNote: Note: you can press Shift during startup for 'Safe mode' to restore defaults and avoid reading or setting anything.
AppMenu.Icon.SliderOnly: Only if at least one slider is present
AppMenu.Icon.ExternalOnly: Only when external display is present
AppMenu.QuitText: Relaunch the app to access Settings if the menu option is not accessible. Use the button below to quit the app.
AppMenu.ShowBrightnessText: Brightness slider for hardware or software controlled displays or TVs.
AppMenu.ShowBuiltIn: Show it for built-in displays as well
AppMenu.ShowBuiltInText: Built-in displays already have a brightness slider in Windows Quick Settings.
AppMenu.DdcOnlyText: For hardware (DDC) controlled displays only. Results may vary.
AppMenu.MultiSliders.Separate: Show separate controls for each display in menu
AppMenu.MultiSliders.Relevant: Show sliders only for the display currently showing the menu
AppMenu.MultiSliders.Combine: Use combined slider for all displays
AppMenu.MultiSliders.CombineText: Works best with various syncing and 'control all' keyboard settings enabled.
AppMenu.SnapText: Slider knob will snap to 0%, 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% when in proximity making setting these values easier. Disable for finer control.
AppMenu.TickMarksText: Show tick marks at 0%, 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% for accuracy.
AppMenu.PercentagesText: Show percentage next to slider for more precision.
Keyboard.MediaBrightnessText: Standard keys are the brightness keys of external keyboards that have them, and Scroll Lock / Pause. Hold Ctrl to adjust the built-in display, Ctrl+Win to adjust external displays. Hold Shift+Alt for fine control. Ctrl+Alt+Win adjusts contrast on DDC compatible displays. Alt opens the Windows display settings.
Keyboard.DisableAltKeys: Do not use alternative brightness keys
Keyboard.DisableAltKeysText: Alternative keys are Scroll Lock and Pause (F14/F15 on Apple keyboards, brightness keys on some Logitech keyboards).
Keyboard.ShortcutsText: Hold Win together with a shortcut for fine control. Laptop brightness keys (Fn) are handled by the computer itself and cannot be used by apps.
Keyboard.Brightness.Focus: Use window focus to determine which display to control
Keyboard.Brightness.FocusText: Using window focus might not work properly with full screen apps.
Keyboard.FineScaleBrightness: Use fine OSD scale for brightness and contrast
Keyboard.FineScaleText: Normally keyboard controls change one OSD chiclet worth of value and Shift+Alt allows fine control. This makes fine control default.
Keyboard.SeparateScale: Separate scales for combined hardware & software dimming
Keyboard.SeparateScaleText: Full OSD scale will be available for hardware brightness control and after reaching 0 brightness, further software dimming will be used.
Keyboard.VolumeMode.Media: Standard keyboard volume and mute keys
Keyboard.Volume.AudioName: Use audio device name to determine which display to control
Keyboard.Volume.MouseText: Works when the sound output is a display (HDMI or DisplayPort audio).
Keyboard.Volume.AudioNameText: You can override audio device name under Displays (advanced) if needed.
Keyboard.FineScaleVolume: Use fine OSD scale for volume
Keyboard.PlayFeedback: Play a sound when the volume is changed
Displays.Warning: ⚠️ Warning! Changing some of these settings may cause system freezes or unexpected behavior!
Displays.LongerDelay: Longer delay during DDC read operations
Displays.Status.Unspecified: This display has an unspecified control status.
Displays.Status.Virtual: This is a virtual display (examples: Miracast, Remote Desktop, a display connected via a DisplayLink dock or similar) which does not allow hardware or software gammatable control. Shading is used as a substitute but only in non-mirror scenarios. Mouse cursor will be unaffected.
Displays.Status.SoftwareOnly: This display allows for software brightness control via gamma table manipulation or shade as it does not support hardware control. Reasons for this might be the display, the cable or adapter, the graphics driver or a dock that does not pass DDC/CI through.
Displays.Status.SoftwareForced: This display is reported to support hardware DDC control but the current settings allow for software control only.
Displays.Status.Ddc: This display is reported to support hardware DDC control. If you encounter issues, you can disable hardware DDC control to force software control.
Displays.Status.Internal: This built-in display supports native Windows brightness control. Windows can also control it without MonitorControl.
Onboarding.Description: Control your external displays brightness, contrast and volume directly from your PC, using the sliders in the notification area or the keyboard.
Onboarding.KeysText: Ctrl+Alt+↑/↓ changes brightness, Ctrl+Alt+→/← changes volume and Ctrl+Alt+M mutes. You can change them in Settings > Keyboard.
Onboarding.StartAtLoginText: Ensure MonitorControl is always running when you need it by launching the app at startup.
